top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice is a distinct, experimentally verified principle: it cancels the light shift so many atoms are interrogated Doppler- and recoil-free, combining ensemble statistics with single-particle systematic control. It has been reproduced independently at several laboratories near 1e-18 and is already yielding physics. The two-name allocation (Katori proposed and first realised it, Ye took it to record accuracy) is defensible, and the citation, if it names the lattice principle and not clock accuracy or the redefinition of the second, answers the 2005 and 2012 overlap. That overlap and the unconfirmed priority record for Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Oates are real reservations, but they do not justify withholding the prize.
